NBA defends refs, Last Two Minute Reports: 'We want to be transparent'

NBA games are a show. The refs don't call a lot of fouls on the final play because the crowd wants an exiting finish. But the refs call/don't call fouls in the second half of most highly watched regular season games to keep games close so fans don't miss any commercials. Coaches even pretend to call timeouts at around the 6-7 minute mark for no other reason than to make you watch commercials. Download the Score app and turn on the Close Game Alert(within 5 points in last 3 minutes) and watch how many times it goes off for popular teams. Players still have to make baskets to win but it's far from a pure sport these days.

Portland Public Schools bans material that casts doubt on climate change

This is not good at all. Science education in public schools is now entering a dogmatic phase. There is enough out there in the scientific literature given failed predictions from climate change scientists to warrant including weak areas of the science that casts doubt on the issue that it is worthy of being included in the test book.
I guess that means that Venice will be censored off the map now...
I hear they have also decided not to buy textbooks that support Young Earth Creationism. It's almost like adhering to scientific reality is a nonnegotiable aspect of public education.

Teaching creationism is not the same thing as teaching climate change as fact - no one was trying to ban teaching climate change as a theory and replace with nonscientific crap. Even evolution is taught as a theory, because "theory" in the scientific context is different than the layman version of the word. It's important in science to distinguish theories and facts, so no, I think what they're doing is being very selective and biased on how climate change is taught. That's not adhering to scientific reality, that's adhering to a biased political agenda.

Climate change is an observable reality, just as evolution is an observable reality. We have hard evidence that the weather patterns are changing, the ice caps melting, etc. We can track the genetic changes in successive generations as colonies of bacteria respond to their environmental conditions.

Now, how it all got started, what's going to happen next, how it's all going to turn out in the end... these are questions that can be investigated using the scientific method, and the various theories scientists have come up with are perfectly appropriate material for a science textbook.

But the essential facts - that life as we know it evolved on this planet over billions of years rather than being seeded in its current forms for by an omnipotent deity 7,000 years ago, that our ecosystem is currently undergoing rapid changes in response to human activity... these are settled questions. The fact that some adherents of our less-sophisticated religious sects either can't or won't accept that should not have any bearing on the material we present to our children in our public schools. Their opinions are irrelevant to the teaching of science, and must not be pandered to. Public schools are supposed to be in the business of imparting knowledge, not perpetuating superstitions.
